cost: THE GATE STEP IS NOT CLOSED, ONLY CUT: at volume 54 the ceiling is still worth 0.26 x (80 - 54) = 6.76 of o_score, so the step from 54 to 55 is a drop of up to 6.76 (6.29 printed OFF, worst case Kevin Love '12's bars) where it used to be 15.05 (14.00 printed, Donyell Marshall '04). Closing it entirely is PROVABLY a class extension: OG Anunoby '21 (pinned 65 +-2, reading 63, zero room down) keeps 11.27 of correction at volume 36, and a monotone law sheds at most 0.26 a volume point, so the payment cannot reach zero before volume 79. A later round that wants the step gone has to accept that lift or move the wall.

THE CEILING'S WINDOW IS [77, 81] AND BOTH EDGES ARE PINS, not taste: at 76 Anunoby '21 falls to 62 and leaves his band; at 82 Rashard Lewis '01 reads 69 and leaves his. 80 is recal_131's PZ_V_HI, the one line the file already has inside the window — but it is written as this term's OWN constant (OB_V_TOP), the way recal_188 wrote SB_SECOND_FULL rather than borrowing recal_163's, so a later re-cut of the paint floor's load ramp does not silently move this ceiling.

WHY A CEILING AND NOT A SHARE. A share of the correction ramped over volume (recal_118's shape, the first form the ruling names) pays the same share to every card at the same volume, and the class holds TWO cards at volume 47 whose rulings point opposite ways: Lewis '01 must shed ten printed points of a 15.58 correction and Marshall '07 must keep all of a 5.45 one. MEASURED: at the share that lands Lewis (0.33) Marshall '07 falls 49 -> 46, three outside his band.

AND A SHARE CANNOT BE MONOTONE. The correction reaches 24 of o_score while the standard path pays volume at 0.26 x load a point, so a share falling to zero anywhere inside ninety volume points takes a card DOWN for carrying more — which is the defect, not the repair.

THE CEILING IS MONOTONE BY CONSTRUCTION: where it binds it falls at exactly 0.26 a volume point, the standard path's own volume weight, while the standard path rises at 0.26 x load plus the signature term's 0.08 x efficiency/100. MEASURED on a volume sweep 0..54 of every card this floor can pay: no added violation reaches half a printed point (worst, Brook Lopez '23, 0.408 of o_score = 0.38 of OFF, off the hub and passer ramps whose own volume slope is under 0.26), and of the cards the ceiling binds on not one is under 25.8 mpg — every one is at recal_96's full load, where the ceiling's slope IS the standard path's own.

MEASURED on the whole pool: 16 of 10,000 cards move on OFF, EVERY ONE OF THEM DOWN, max -7, mean -2.44; OVR follows on 13, max -5; DEF and every attribute move on ZERO. The top 12 by OFF is identical name for name and the top 50 by OVR has no entrant and no leaver. 215 anchors (this round adds two), 0 failing.

The movers are one archetype and read like it — the full-time stretch big who was carrying a real share of the offence and being paid as an off-ball specialist anyway: Marshall '04, Lewis '01 and '10, LaFrentz '02, Brook Lopez '23, Radmanović '04, Parsons '15, Markkanen '21, Hachimura '25, Frye '11, Collins '26, Anunoby '25 and '26, the two Finney-Smith seasons, Keegan Murray '24.
